title: fix(studio): conditional formatting refuses == on a list field while typing
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8M6sbZjBjat5VcHCF9RcSaz)_

Fixes #36459

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 在视图的「条件格式」里，管理员写「标签等于 VIP」这类把多选字段当单值比较的规则时，编辑框会当场标红并给出改写建议（改成「VIP 在标签里」），保存按钮在改好之前不放行；以前这种规则能存下来，但永远不会给任何一行上色。
- 属于界面体验专题，是「多选字段不能用等于比较」这一修复（字段属性面板已做）在条件格式编辑器上的补齐。
- 出错的话只是条件格式编辑框多报或少报一条提示，不改已有视图和数据，可直接撤回。
- 无。

## What changes

`CelPredicateField` has taken the object's field definitions (`fieldDefs`: name, `type`, `multiple`) since the field inspector's list-equality work: it reads the list-valued fields through `isMultiValueField` and hands them to the lint as `multiValueFields`, so the engine refuses `record.LISTFIELD == 'x'` (`list-equality`) with the membership rewrite. The view conditional formatting editor mounted one `CelPredicateField` per rule but never passed `fieldDefs`, so no field was judged a list there and such a rule linted clean, saved, and never matched a row.

- `ConditionalFormattingEditor` takes an optional `fieldDefs` prop and hands it to every rule's `CelPredicateField`. Omitted, the lint is what it was.
- Both mount sites pass it: `ViewVariantInspector` (metadata admin view page) builds it from the `useObjectFields` catalog it already reads; `ListViewMoreSection` (Studio list-view panel) builds it from the loaded `fieldCatalog` it already receives, which already carries `multiple`.
- The refusal is an `error`, so it counts in the editor's existing blocking-issue report: the host's Save (metadata admin) and autosave hold (Studio panel) stay shut until the rule is rewritten.

No spec, rule shape or server change. `ConditionalFormattingEditor` is not in `@object-ui/app-shell`'s published exports, so no export changes (Clause-② no). Changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch.

Card item 2 (should the view save refuse the same shape) is dropped by the seat; see Acceptance notes.

## Tests

New file `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ConditionalFormattingEditor.listEquality-36459.test.tsx`, against the real `@objectstack/formula` engine:

- editor: `record.tags == 'vip'` and `record.tags != 'vip'` on a `select` declared `multiple: true` show the "holds a list" finding with the `in` rewrite and report 1 blocking issue;
- editor: `'vip' in record.tags` is clean (0 blocking);
- control: `record.stage == 'open'` on a single-value `select` is clean;
- mount sites: the view variant inspector (fed `objectFieldsOverride`) and the Studio list-view panel (fed a loaded `fieldCatalog`) both show the finding; the panel reports 1 blocking issue.

Reverse verification at `7c65f8b9`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 → 0, blob changed, restored blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty): with the `fieldDefs={fieldDefs}` pass-through deleted from `ConditionalFormattingEditor`, the 4 refusing cases fail and the 2 clean cases pass.

## Acceptance notes

- Card item 2 (the view save refusing the same shape): dropped — new save-door lint site; new gates default no. On `main` a view's `conditionalFormatting[].condition` is not CEL-linted at save at all (`validate-expressions` lints a field's own `conditionalFormatting`; the `view` write path runs the bulk-confirm text pass only), so refusing it there would be a new gate. Not filed.

## Verification

Read first:
1. `ConditionalFormattingEditor.tsx`: the new `fieldDefs` prop and its pass-through to `CelPredicateField`.
2. `ListViewMoreSection.tsx`: `fieldDefs` built from `fieldCatalog` only when it is loaded (riskiest hunk: `undefined` while loading means no list judgement until the catalog arrives).
3. `ViewVariantInspector.tsx`: `celFieldDefs` from the same catalog the field name list comes from.

Two-minute check: in Studio, open a list view of an object with a multi-select field, add a conditional formatting rule and type `record.FIELD == 'x'` for that field: the box shows "holds a list" with the `in` rewrite and the view does not save; type `'x' in record.FIELD`: the finding clears.
